claims.text: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's COO from 2022 until an April 2026 reorganization moved him into a special-projects role reporting to Sam Altman, announced on 11 August 2026 via his own post that he is leaving OpenAI entirely, saying he is departing to 'start something new'
claims.reasoning: Independently reported same-day by TechCrunch, CNBC and Fortune, each with distinct bylines quoting Lightcap's own announcement post rather than relaying a single wire story or press release -- clears the >=2-independent-source business-claim bar. TechCrunch's piece, fetched in full, states directly that he moved to special projects earlier in 2026 during an executive reorganization, correcting an initial framing (carried from the candidate entry) that would have called him the sitting COO. Falsifier specifically checked for and found no denial, correction or retraction.

claims.text: OpenAI announced on 13 August 2026 that Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser -- in the role since December 2025 -- is leaving to pursue other opportunities, and named Dali Rajic, formerly president and COO of Wiz, as her successor
claims.reasoning: Tier-0 primary: OpenAI's own site post (openai.com/index/dali-rajic-chief-revenue-officer/) names Rajic as Dresser's successor and states Dresser is leaving to pursue other opportunities; confirmed via a site-scoped search after direct fetch returned HTTP 403 (a listed known blocker this run). Independently corroborated same-day by CNBC, TechCrunch and Bloomberg with distinct bylines and reporting detail (e.g. Bloomberg's 'after less than a year' framing, TechCrunch's enterprise-revenue context), not a single relayed scoop.

notes: Verifier and falsifier both confirmed this is unrelated to the still-watching openai-safety-heidecke-departure ledger entry (that one covers a safety-org reshuffle -- Mia Glaese/Saachi Jain -- single-sourced to a Wired exclusive); no outlet connects the two threads.
